language_ml_001_naati_policy.text: For Malayalam CCL, NAATI recognises regional variations and dialects. A candidate is not penalised merely
merely for using a Kerala regional dialect as long as the language would be understood by an average
by an average Malayalee living in Kerala.

in Kerala.
Malayalam has adopted words from several languages, including English. Limited use of English words
English words may be acceptable when the word is conventionally used and widely understood, particularly in
particularly in scientific, medical and technical contexts or where an accurate Malayalam translation is

is unavailable.
Where a commonly used Malayalam equivalent exists, NAATI prefers the Malayalam term.

For
For numbers, NAATI's Malayalam policy expects numbers to be rendered in Malayalam rather than simply repeated in
numerals. Figures expressed in millions should be converted appropriately to lakhs/crores and vice versa.
This is a Malayalam-specific policy. As additional CCL languages are introduced into Way2Australia, each language
each language should have its own official language-policy document rather than applying Malayalam rules globally.

official_001_ccl_format_scoring_results.text: The NAATI Credentialed Community Language (CCL) test assesses the ability to interpret community conversations

- each dialogue is worth 45 marks;
- total available marks: 90;
- pass requirement: at least 63/90 overall and at least 29/45 in each dialogue.
A candidate can therefore fail even with an overall score of 63 or more if one dialogue is below 29.
NAATI uses a deduction-based assessment approach.
Important areas include accuracy, language quality/register and delivery.
Candidates must begin interpreting within five seconds of the chime.
Excessive pauses, repeated corrections and excessive segment repeats can result in deductions.
Official CCL results are normally sent by email within 4–6 weeks.
CCL is not professional interpreter or translator certification.

official_002_candidate_rules_setup.text: Current NAATI candidate instructions include these key requirements:
- The official test is completed on a computer or laptop.
- A separate phone or tablet is used as part of online proctoring.
- Headsets, headphones and earphones are not allowed.

- Notes may be taken with a pen and blank loose sheets of paper.
- Prepared notes, electronic
electronic resources, typed notes, dictionaries, browsing, live captions and transcription tools are

are prohibited.
- The test performance recording must remain under 20 minutes; navigation/setup time is separate.
- The candidate should begin interpreting within five seconds after the chime.
- One repeated segment per dialogue is allowed without penalty; additional repeats may attract deductions.
- Self-correction is permitted, but excessive pauses/corrections can affect delivery.

- Interpretation should use direct/first-person speech; indirect third-person reporting is not acceptable.
- The
- The system check must be completed at least 48 hours before the test using the same intended computer,
computer, phone, location and internet connection.

connection.
- Technical incidents related to the official test should be reported to NAATI within 24 hours.
Always direct users to the live NAATI candidate instructions for current requirements.
